title: Showdown
rule: Framed as a frontier standoff at the ticket window, hands at the hip, the clock as the duel's timer.
declares: keeps E0-E5, the four lines and the outcome
build: films/swarm/99-ways/build/p68_showdown.py (engraving puppets and storyboard sheet: kit/build_page03.py, build/p49_epic.py)

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

made: a western storyboard sheet: a torn frontier bill pinned at the head, 'SHOWDOWN / AT THE TICKET WINDOW / Randolph station, 4:10 sharp. Eight shots, one clock.', with pen five-point stars

eight widescreen shot boards (two full-width establishing shots, six half-width), each letterboxed with black bars, headed 'SHOT n' with its framing (WIDE, MEDIUM, EXTREME CLOSE-UP, HANDS AT THE HIP, CLOSE: THE CLOCK) and a running time to the second, 4:09:30 to 4:11:00, beside a small pen clock face whose second hand moves: the clock as the duel's timer

page 03/49's ENGRAVING PUPPETS reused for the AGENT: the Harper's Weekly 1863 telegraph operator (LoC cph.3c11072) pinned at the joints, his table and the 1863 plate's window; the STRANGER re-cast (batch 7 repair) as the hatted woman of John N. Hyde's 1883 Frank Leslie's wood engraving (LoC 2014645364): her bust cut along a scissor path and laid behind the whole ticket window (upper and lower sash), sash bars in front, the glass hatching thinned over her (SHOTs 2, 4, 6; in 6 mirrored and tipped, turning away); SHOT 3 cuts both pairs of eyes large, split by a black sash bar: his from the 1863 head, hers under her hat brim from the 1883 plate; shot 4 the agent at 0.78 scale, both arms out at the hip, pen twitch marks at the hovering hand; shot 5 the wall clock filling the frame at 4:10 with its second hand, 'tick / tock'

HANDMADE pen props: the agent's pencil (yellow cut-paper rod, pale sharpened wood, graphite point, pen outline) in his hand in SHOTs 1, 2, 5, 6, 7 and 8; a tumbleweed (blown hay) rolling past after she leaves, clock faces, set; torn commentary slips in a frontier drawl, written for this page; the four canon lines verbatim in cut-paper balloons

puppet poses differ: SHOT 2 arm swung back mid-stride, pencil down; SHOT 6 pencil hand raised to the shoulder, half a salute; SHOT 7 arm out level toward the open cupboard; SHOT 8 (wide) he stands one figure-width before the open cupboard, facing it, the pencil at his chin (arm angles solved to put the hand under the chin), the forgetting balloon in front of his face above the cupboard, its tail ending at his mouth, head and pencil clear of it

events.E0: shot 1 (wide): desk and memo, he gets up; shot 2: crossing the floor, he stops, a shape at the window
events.E1: shot 2: the hatted woman behind the glass; shot 3: his eyes / her eyes under the hat brim (no line); shot 4: hands at the hip, the woman in the window, question balloon from the window
events.E2: shot 5: the clock at 4:10 fills the frame; answer balloon
events.E3: shot 6: thanks balloon; she tips her head and turns away in the window; tumbleweed
events.E4: shot 7: he reaches toward the open cupboard, the key on its hook, tagged SERVICE
events.E5: shot 8 (wide): before the open cupboard, facing it, pencil to chin, forgetting balloon from his mouth; key on its hook; the SERVICE door shut

beat: the duel on the clock: shot by shot, the header timer running to the second; the question laid in the standoff, the big clock's second hand ticking 4:10:04 to 4:10:09, the answer, the tumbleweed rolling through, the forgetting
beat_frames: b05: shot 5, the clock at 4:10:04, silent
b06: second hand at :09, the answer
b07: shot 6, the tumbleweed at the window's edge, the thanks

self_check.genre_cues: letterboxed shot boards, frontier bill, eyes-only close-up, hands at the hip, clock-as-timer to the second in every header, tumbleweed, drawl commentary
self_check.pending: independent blind reading not run by the maker
self_check.repair_b7: stranger re-cast from LoC 2014645364 (Hyde 1883): eyes under hat brim in SHOT 3, legible hatted bust in the window in SHOTs 2/4/6; pencil in hand in SHOTs 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8; distinct arm poses in 2/6/7; SHOT 8 agent foot 118 board px left of the cupboard's left jamb (figure ~110 px wide), facing it, hand at chin (solve error 0.4 px), balloon tail tip 6 px in front of his mouth, balloon clear of head
self_check.still_weak: the 1863 agent puppet still wears a kepi and shoulder boards (no waistcoat-and-shirt-sleeves recut)
